title: Global Virtual School (GVS)
summary: Enhancing access to and refining English-language skills training in some of the most economically disadvantaged and underserved regions worldwide.
description:
The General ESL (English as a Second Language) and the EAP (English for Academic Purposes) programs by Global Virtual School are dedicated to enhancing access to and refining English-language skills training in some of the most economically disadvantaged and underserved regions worldwide. In these areas, acquiring proficient English-language skills serves as a means to break the cycle of generational poverty. The program actively advocates for gender equality, maintaining an admission policy that ensures a fifty-percent female representation in every learning space.

Furthermore, the program actively cultivates Global Competence by urging learners, even in remote villages, to challenge themselves in mastering language proficiency and achieving a native-speaker level of English. The trusted Cambridge IGCSE curriculum supports students in advancing their English proficiency to an advanced level, equipping them for successful careers or further education. Through the utilization of past papers, students undergo assessments to ensure they are aligned with global standards and comparable to their peers worldwide.

Global Virtual School (GVS) offers learners a non-traditional classroom setting, fostering the development of critical thinking and problem-solving skills that are not typically emphasized in traditional educational settings but are highly valued in the job market. The youth-to-youth connection establishes a supportive learning atmosphere, enhancing learner confidence.

### Current Impact
In collaboration with partners like the US State Department and University of Central Asia, GVS connects volunteer-teachers with eager learners in real-time virtual classrooms. GVS aims to graduate over 5,000 proficient English speakers by 2025, empowering them to escape generational poverty. At present, GVS has significant impact in 14 countries and 30 centers where it equips over 1300 students with the language skills needed to pursue higher education, vocational training, and improved career prospects.

### Locations
India, Tajikistan, Afghanistan, Kyrgyzstan, Nepal, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Guinea, Cabo Verde, Senegal, Mauritania, Niger, Bangladesh, Uzbekistan.

title: Vocational Skill Training Program, Jaipur India
summary: Empowering youth with practical skills for the modern workforce in Jaipur.
description:
Location: Jaipur, Rajasthan, India
Status: Implemented
Duration: December 2018 – July 2020

### Project Description
The Worldwide Education Fund (WEF) in collaboration with Edu-Girls and Vimukti Sanstha embarked on a transformative project aimed at empowering deserving girls from minority communities. With a generous grant of $10,000 from WEF, the initiative focused on providing vocational training scholarships to 26 girls, fostering financial independence and breaking the cycle of generational poverty.

Targeting an average family income of less than Rs 8,350 ($121) per month for families with an average size of 5, Vimukti Sanstha identified courses such as Beautician, Nursery Teachers Training, Apparel Design, etc., tailored to the aptitude of each girl. Through joint counseling and assessment, the selected girls were admitted and supported under these programs, which included not only the training itself but also transportation assistance.

The overarching vision of the project is to equip these girls with essential skill sets, enabling them to thrive in their chosen fields and secure a respectable source of income. Beyond the immediate impact on the individuals involved, the initiative aspires to create a ripple effect, ensuring that these girls become valuable contributors to the workforce, thereby uplifting themselves and their communities.

title: Worldwide Education Fund –Vocational Training (WEF-VT) Scholars Program at Emeralde
summary: A scalable model for vocational education across multiple regions.
description:
Location: Mariam Zaveri’s Emeralde International Institute of Hair and Beauty located in Bandra, Mumbai
Status: Implemented
Duration: October 2015 – May 2016

### Project Description
Launched in October 2015, the WEF-VT Scholars Program at Emeralde is an impactful initiative by the WEF Student Ambassador Association (ISAA) in collaboration with the Foundation to Support Education Worldwide (FSEW), Emeralde International Institute of Hair and Beauty, and FEEB Unlimited. Responding to the increasing demand for candidates with vocational and technical skills, the program awarded full scholarships to deserving individuals in suburban Mumbai and rural Gujarat.

Successful recipients underwent a transformative experience, benefiting from a full scholarship to Mariam Zaveri’s Emeralde International Institute of Hair and Beauty. The 6-month professional course in hair and beauty, along with a certification in skin-peel technology, equipped these young girls with foundational skills for a lifetime. This initiative not only enabled them to contribute financially to their families but also served as a trampoline, helping them break free from the cycle of generational poverty.

As a gesture of support, each candidate received a token kit of tools of the trade from the Worldwide Education Fund at the end of the program. All students have successfully graduated, with some already securing positions as beauticians in local parlors. WEF congratulates these graduates on their achievements, marking a significant step toward a brighter and more empowered future.

title: Computers To UCA-SPCE
summary: Providing essential hardware to support advanced technological learning.
description:
Location: Khorog, Tajikistan
Status: Implemented
Duration: September 2017 – September 2018

### Project Description
The Worldwide Education Fund of  The Dallas Foundation, has generously contributed to the University of Central Asia School of Professional and Continuing Education (UCA-SPCE). Following last year’s donation of 10 high-speed desktop computers, WEF has recently added 11 more, enhancing the capacity and efficiency of the computer lab at UCA-SPCE.

The primary goal of this initiative is to broaden the scope of education by utilizing these computers to offer classes to students who may face challenges accessing UCA-SPCE’s facilities. This expansion aims to provide enhanced teaching options, ensuring educational opportunities reach a wider audience.

Aligned with the scholarship program’s vision, the project anticipates that graduates will benefit from a cutting-edge facility in Khorog, making a meaningful impact on society. Moreover, the computer lab, equipped with high-speed computers, serves as a platform for certified teachers trained through WEF scholarships to conduct Emerging Technology courses. This strategic collaboration between WEF and UCA-SPCE underscores a commitment to advancing education and empowering students for a technology-driven future.

title: Khorog Advanced English Language Course
summary: Elevating language proficiency for better global opportunities.
description:
Location: Khorog, Tajikistan
Status: Implemented

### Project Description
In partnership with the local NGO “Partner+Transfers,” the Worldwide Education Fund of the Dallas Foundation initiated a collaborative effort to enhance the IELTS scores of college-bound students in Khorog town. This project, catering to the unique challenges of the geographically isolated Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Region (GBAO), aimed to address the lack of IELTS preparation courses in the area.

Identifying the need for accessible language proficiency programs, the project selected 20 students through an assessment test, conducting classes five days a week in Khorog. The curriculum, designed to provide a comprehensive approach, focused on enhancing skills in speaking, listening, reading, and writing for the IELTS exam.

The significance of IELTS (International English Language Testing System) as a gateway to global opportunities cannot be overstated. For students in GBAO, the harsh weather conditions and geographical isolation often restrict access to such courses, typically available only in Dushanbe. This advanced English Language Course not only bridged this gap but also empowered students to prepare for the IELTS exam right at their doorstep, eliminating financial barriers and fostering educational opportunities in the region.

title: Herzing University Scholarship 2017-2019
summary: Full-ride scholarships enabling outstanding students to study abroad.
description:
Location: India, Pakistan, and Tajikistan
Status: Implemented
Duration: 2017-2019

### Herzing University Scholarship 2017 – 2019
The WEF-Herzing University-MBA Scholarship, a program by the Worldwide Education Fund (WEF) in collaboration with Herzing University, aims to provide educational opportunities for disadvantaged students in India, Pakistan, and Tajikistan. The scholarship enables qualified recipients to enroll in Herzing University’s MBA program, either at campuses in Atlanta, Georgia, or Madison, Wisconsin, or through online courses in their home countries. The scholarship covers MBA tuition fees, while accommodation expenses during the program are covered by WEF. However, travel costs, book expenses, and monthly stipends are not included.

Intended for hardworking postgraduate students with a strong command of English, the scholarship seeks to empower individuals who aspire to transform their lives and contribute to reshaping the economic future of their home countries. The WEF-Herzing University Scholars Cohort 2017-2019 successfully launched the MBA Scholarship Program, with ten selected students, six of whom have already commenced their studies in Atlanta, GA. These students, representing marginalized communities in Tajikistan and Pakistan, receive full-tuition scholarships from Herzing University, along with residential scholarships from WEF. The program also includes special career mentoring sessions, aiming to cultivate these students as catalysts for economic and social uplift in their communities.

title: Global Learners Capacity Building Project
summary: Enhancing educational infrastructure and teaching methodologies globally.
description:
Location: Houston, Texas USA
Status: Implemented
Duration: June 2018-May 2019

### Project Description
The Worldwide Education Fund (WEF) partnered with the Partnership for the Advancement and Immersion of Refugees (PAIR) to launch a project aimed at engaging refugee youth in educational mentoring after-school programs. Through the integration of app-based literacy, numeracy, tutoring, and enrichment programs, the Global Learners initiative serves over 100 refugee students from three Houston Independent School District (HISD) middle schools with significant refugee populations.

Targeting schools like Las Americas Newcomer School, Jane Long Academy, and Revere Middle School, where students lack personal computers and individual access to laptops, the Global Learners program addressed the limited capacity to effectively use web-based educational software. The project incorporated 18 tablets, with six assigned to each program, facilitating tutoring, research, and computer literacy components.

During academic/tutoring time, English and math app-based tutoring programs were integrated into the program, allowing students to use tablets for homework that required internet access. The tablets were also equipped with learning apps to help students practice English and math skills during homework time. In the last quarter, 68% of students reported using the tablets for homework, math or English apps, or both, with 43% using them at least once a week at PAIR. This initiative underscores WEF’s commitment to bridging educational gaps and providing essential resources for refugee youth in Houston.

title: Technology Upgrades For Head Heart Hands (H3) Program

description:
Location: Dallas Texas, USA
Status: Implemented
Duration: September 2017 – September 2018

### Project Description
WEF collaborates with Hearth House to empower refugee children with technology education. Recognizing the limited access to technology in their backgrounds, this initiative aims to upgrade outdated resources, offering students the opportunity to engage in diverse disciplines like online research, typing, coding, and website creation. These practical skills level the playing field, enhancing readiness for higher academic pursuits and future employment.

The technology infusion will bolster the core program at Hearth House, known as the Head, Heart, and Hands (H3) program. Focused on cognitive learning, character development, and building self-esteem, H3 offers academic support, play therapy, and social-emotional programming. The grant initiative targets 60 students, providing them with a pathway to future success through enhanced technological resources and comprehensive educational support.

title: Sakina of Project Hunza & Gilgit Baltistan Secondary Scholarship
summary: Providing scholarships and professional development for girls in Hunza and Baltistan.
description:
Location: Hunza and Baltistan, Pakistan

### Project Description
WEF’s contributions to the Iqra Fund institution consist of providing secondary and higher school scholarships and professional development sessions offered to all 56 girls living in the various communities of the Hunza and Baltistan regions. The WEF program targets areas that experience harsh weather conditions, lack of infrastructure, and an overwhelming poverty population size. They believe that areas as such are in desperate need of educational funding since most families earn a low income and rely on subsistence farming. The Hunza and Baltistan regions receive no government support; thus, most children residing there are stripped of their educational rights. In addition to the difficulty of obtaining an education, families who can afford schooling often don’t send their children due to the costs of lodging and transportation. WEF recognizes these difficulties and uses them as motivation to fund schooling and all other expenses for innocent children who deserve a pathway to a sustainable education. As a result, WEF has partnered with the Iqra Fund to ensure these children can reach their full potential in all educational aspects.

### Meet Sakina
Now, Sakina is thriving in high school in Skardu and aspires to become a doctor to serve her community. She also feels that by becoming a doctor, she will be able to encourage her community to enable their girls to follow their dreams, the way her parents did for her.

“Girls in my village have a lot of potential, but they live a very hard life of work at home and in the fields, and all their potential go to waste. I want to show them they can achieve their dreams, like me”.

title: Literacy Program at St. Placid’s School, Chittagong, Bangladesh
summary: A targeted intervention to boost foundational literacy skills.
description:
Location: Chittagong, Bangladesh
Status: Active

### Project Description
The main goal of the Literacy Program is to educate individuals from economically disadvantaged backgrounds, enabling them to break the cycle of generational poverty. Three organizations with shared values have come together to champion this initiative: the Old Placidian Association (OPA), the Foundation to Support Education Worldwide (FSEW) based in the USA, and the Worldwide Education Fund of The Dallas Foundation (WEF), also based in the USA.

Through a collaborative agreement, WEF, FSEW, and OPA are joining forces to enrich the Literacy Program. This partnership involves providing advisory services and the necessary funding to expand the current program, aiming to make a significant impact on the educational opportunities available to individuals from underprivileged families.

### Current Impact
Presently, the Old Placidian Association (OPA) oversees a Literacy Program for 250 underserved boys in Chittagong, Bangladesh, up to the 5th grade. There is a recognized necessity to extend the program’s reach, expanding it from the 5th standard to the 10th standard.

description:

title: Digital Marketing Assistant Program, Tajikistan
summary: Empowering young people through specialized e-commerce and digital skills.
description:
Location: Tajikistan
Status: Active

### Project Description
This comprehensive initiative focuses on delivering Digital Marketing courses at UCA-SPCE through certified facilitators, mirroring the successful model established for the Cyber Security course. With the overarching goal of creating employment opportunities for youth in Central Asia, the project adopts a “train the trainer” approach. Qualified candidates with teaching skills and an IT background are identified, certifying themselves and committing to two years of teaching at local learning institutions. Following certification, these facilitators will collaborate with UCA-SPCE to initiate Digital Marketing Assistant Courses, and subsequently, UCA-SPCE will employ them to teach online.

![Flowchart](programs/completed projects/Digital Marketing Assistant Program, Tajikistan Flowchart.png)

To ensure accessibility, the courses will be integrated into UCA’s Learning Management System (LMS), enabling online training for students in Afghanistan and Northern Pakistan. The chosen facilitators will undergo a digital marketing certification course offered by Shaw Academy (https://www.shawacademy.com/en-us/).

The project’s Proof of Concept Execution Plan includes connecting graduates with emerging digital marketing skills to opportunities in IT services and consulting companies, thereby fostering a comprehensive approach to skill development and sustainable employment in the region.

title: Early Childhood Development Centre, Pakistan
summary: Fostering optimal growth through specialized Montessori environments.
description:
Location: Chitral, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan
Status: Active

### Project Description
The mission of the Worldwide Education Fund (WEF), USA is to create and support Early Childhood Development Programs in underserved communities across South and Central Asian countries. In these regions, existing educational systems struggle to meet the developmental needs of children under the age of 6.

WEF collaborates with both governmental and non-governmental organizations to establish Early Childhood Development (ECD) centers. These centers provide a dedicated space where children aged 3-5 can gather in an environment designed to foster their optimal growth. The facilities are equipped with specialized furniture, tools, and materials, all aimed at stimulating the children’s physical, socio-emotional, and intellectual development.

Trained Montessori Teachers play a crucial role in these centers, guiding and facilitating the children’s learning experiences. The goal is to enhance the children’s senses and promote their overall development during these foundational years. Through these efforts, WEF aims to make a positive impact on the lives of young children in marginalized communities, setting the stage for a brighter future.

### Current Impact
Situated at a low-cost private school, our Early Childhood Development Centre, Chitral, stands out as the first of its kind to embrace the Montessori Method of learning. We pride ourselves on being fully equipped with ECD materials that align with the core philosophy of Maria Montessori. Our dedicated teachers are certified by the Pakistan Montessori Council, ensuring a commitment to excellence.

At our ECD Centre, we are breaking away from traditional teaching and learning methods. We emphasize parent participation by providing opportunities for them to attend parent teaching sessions, engage in classroom observations, and participate in storytelling activities.

Currently, the center accommodates 40 children aged 3-5 years in two sessions, fostering a student-centered learning experience. Over the past three years, our ECD Centre has successfully graduated 60 students, and we eagerly anticipate making a positive impact on even more young minds in the future.

title: WEF-HU MBA PROGRAM SCHOLARS MEHRUNISSA BARKATALI
summary: A blog by WEF-HU MBA Scholar Mehrunissa Barkatali about her transformative experience.
description:
Location: Karachi, Pakistan

### Blog by Mehrunissa Barkatali
This blog is written by WEF-HU MBA Scholar Mehrunissa Barkatali who is currently doing her 4th Semester in Herzing University Atlanta, USA. She is originally from Karachi, Pakistan. The WEF-HU MBA Scholarship Program is a unique chance to experience something amazing. Applying for this scholarship had changed my life forever. I did not know what an amazing journey was waiting for me. When I came to the US everything was new, like the host family. It is unreal. I cannot forget the first meeting at the airport and the first hug from people who were going to be your “second” family forever. Then I was living, adjusting and becoming a part of this family. Only by being a student, I learned such things as being responsible, thinking ahead and how appreciating all, that I had. When you live in another country, you start forming a new life opinion.The biggest thing I have learned during staying in the US, was how to be an adult.

My year in America helped me to grow up and see things differently. That is really important to me. My host family, my university (Herzing University) became a part of my life forever and I will never forget the experience of becoming the part of the family, traveling together or participating at school. This new environment really helped me to find something new, that I can love and connect to my life for a long time. Thank you.
